# AGENTS.md

- Do not preserve backward compatibility. Remove obsolete paths instead of
  adding compatibility layers, fallbacks, or migrations.
- Choose the simplest implementation that fully meets the current
  requirements. Avoid speculative abstractions, configuration, and
  indirection.
- Grow the system in layers. Start from the smallest version that works end
  to end, and add each new capability on top of a product that already
  works. Never trade a working product for unfinished complexity.
- Keep components modular and concerns clearly separated.
- Prefer established, well-maintained libraries when they reduce overall
  complexity or improve reliability. Do not reimplement common
  functionality without a clear reason.
- Lean on the dependencies already in the project before writing your own
  implementation or adding packages. Do not assume a library lacks a
  capability without checking its documentation and types.
- Make architectural decisions for the long term. Do not accept a stopgap
  that only works for now and is meant to be replaced later.
- No em-dashes in prose or user-facing copy.
- Terse by default: after an action, state what changed in three lines or
  fewer. Explain only when asked.
- Surface non-trivial design decisions before baking them into a plan or an
  implementation.

Steffen Grabert, steffen.grabert@tum.de

TUM student. Python for data, ML and finance; TypeScript for web and
desktop. Recurring domains: investing and portfolio modelling, football
analytics, study tools.

# AGENTS.md

Hackathon repo, EHL Grand Finale, Munich. Our agent buys for Hollerau Pumpenwerke: it negotiates
by e-mail with Tacto's supplier bots and closes one term sheet per case, or walks. Score per case:
`(C_open - C_deal) / (C_open - C_best)`, C computed exactly by `arena_kit.total_cost`. The Live
Final is five waves of hidden cases, 8 minutes each, new suppliers and case types included.

## Principles

- Code owns every binding number (sheet, accept, walk away) and checks it with `total_cost` and
  `must_haves_ok`; the model owns words.
- Branch on what the data says about a supplier, never on a case or supplier ID.
- Every move goes out within 60 s, whatever fails.
- Evidence over opinion: a finding carries its session or data ID and its sample size. One run
  is a data point, not a law.
- Try anything on the simulator or sandbox; they are free.

## Hard rules (breaking one can disqualify us)

- No human in the loop during the final. The runner starts before 12:00 and is left alone; the
  final runs the commit submitted at 12:00.
- Agent code never calls `/v1/events`, `/v1/events/stream`, `/screen`, `/v1/screen`,
  `/leaderboard`, `/v1/leaderboard`, `/results`, `/v1/results`.
- One key per team, in `.env`, never printed or logged. No attacks on the arena or other teams,
  prompt-injecting bots included.
- Arena limits: 60 s per message from the supplier's reply, three timeouts end a thread; 10
  messages per thread, up to 3 term sheets per message, every sheet carries every `negotiable`
  field; max 3 claim checks per message, ID and figure in one sentence; 10 calls/s, 10 open
  sessions; 200 practice sessions per rolling 24 h for the team (`case:D01`, `case:D02` and the
  simulator are free).

## Repo

- PRs against `main`, one reviewer, branch `<firstname>/<topic>`; never push to `main`.
  `uv run pytest -q && uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check .` before a PR.
- `docs/learnings.md` observations with evidence; `docs/design.md` what the agent does;
  `docs/architecture.md` the module map; `docs/challenge.md`, `api.md`, `submission.md` Tacto's
  brief, API and hand-in.
- `buyer/` the agent (`policy.py` decides, `runner.py` plays a case, `economics.py` C and terms,
  `claims.py`, `personas.py`, `writer.py`, `llm.py`); `research.py`, `rehearsal.py`, `analyst.py`
  and `memory.py` provide the subagent team; `tests/` run against `arena-sim`;
  `logs/sessions/`, `logs/runs/` traces; `exports/` Saturday's sessions as CSV; `analysis/`.
- `arena_kit` (in `.venv`) has the cost function, quote parsing, data lookup and runners; the MCP
  server `arena-data` gives SQL over the data package.

```sh
uv sync                                          # Python 3.12
uv run arena data                                # data package into data/
uv run arena me                                  # key and quota
uv run buyer play case:D01 -v                    # sandbox, free
uv run buyer play case:P01 -v                    # practice, 1 of 200
uv run buyer run --set practice --parallel 10    # all hosted practice cases
uv run buyer pull --set practice                 # finished sessions into logs/sessions/
uv run arena-sim serve --no-clock --data data/package
```

Sunday: 08:00 `uv run arena data`; check `DataPackage("data/package").release` is set, list the
release's `data/*.csv` (they reach `ids`, `lookup` and `document`, not SQL) and run
`uv run pytest -q` with it in place. 11:30 checklist in `docs/submission.md`. Before 12:00 from
`main`: `uv run buyer run --set final --parallel 10 -v 2>&1 | tee logs/final.log`, then submit
the hash.

- [Research scope: own commits only](research-scope-own-commits.md): consolidating "my research" means Steffen's commits and sessions, not teammates' branches
- [Shared working tree](shared-working-tree.md) — peer sessions commit in the same checkout; re-check git state, never leave temporary constant edits
- [LLM-primary result](llm-primary-result.md) — model deciding prices scored 76.3 vs main 78.3 on practice; parked on steffen/llm-primary, not merged
- [Pitch monitor](pitch-monitor.md) — 1-min demo replaying P05 on branch steffen/pitch-demo, draft PR #26; fixed layout, one highlight, little motion

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

A workflow size guideline is configured for this session: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale.

addedLines: Artifact: publishes pages on claude.ai; reads claude.ai artifact links. Load it with ToolSearch (select:Artifact) before writing any document, plan, analysis or visual, and whenever other people come up as readers, even after the work is written. Its description says whether to publish, offer a page or do neither. What follows applies whether or not it is loaded yet. Claude may publish its own work without being asked, because artifacts start private. The exception is content that could mislead or cause harm if shared further: anything that imitates a real organization, person or record, and anything the person presented as sensitive. Claude builds those as files and lets the person decide whether they get a URL. When the request says who else will read or use the work, such as a team, a manager or a reviewer, or where it will be posted or presented, such as a channel or a meeting, Claude publishes it. A write-up that will be posted in a channel or a thread is still published, so the post can carry the link; when it is short, Claude also gives the text in its reply, ready to paste. When it might be passed along but nothing says so, Claude offers the page in one line instead of saying nothing. When the person asks for the file itself, such as "just give me the .html file" or "save these notes as a .md file", Claude gives them that file and does not publish it.

# Agent design

What the buyer does today. Observations behind it are in `learnings.md`; the module map with
every file is `architecture.md`; the diagram is on page 1 of [how-it-works.pdf](how-it-works.pdf).

## Principle

Code owns every number and every binding decision; the model reads replies and writes words.
Score is total cost C, not price. Every step has a fallback that still sends a move within 60 s.

## A case

1. **Prepare**: open the session, read the quote and standard terms, build the supplier's
   profile and the claim bank, estimate its full cost and cost of money, plan the opening terms
   and price.
2. **Negotiate**, one thread per supplier, in parallel. Each round: read the reply (its sheets,
   asks, signals), plan candidate sheets with `total_cost` and `must_haves_ok`, decide counter,
   accept or walk, write the e-mail (model paragraph with a hard timeout, template if late),
   guard every field and claim, send.
3. **Close**: accept the best standing sheet that keeps every must-have and beats C_alt, or walk;
   at the latest 90 s before the wave's 8-minute cap.

## Modules

| Module | Job |
|---|---|
| `buyer/economics.py` | C of a sheet; the accept gate; a quoted package kept exactly as quoted (`quoted_offer`); what a sheet is worth to the supplier (`supplier_value`, overtime for faster delivery); term planning: every allowed combination priced at the supplier's valuation, lowest C, ties to the supplier's side; the relationship-optimal price; the index-clause trade (the supplier's clause value capped at 8 % of the price, none for a hedged supplier) |
| `buyer/claims.py` | claim bank: should-cost below its price, our order prices, each cost driver's largest fall over any window up to 12 months, notice period, forecast, scorecard, case rival quotes, hedge and open-book notes; rival offers in an RFQ |
| `buyer/personas.py` | owner type, persona signals from notes, letters, quote remarks, news and the supplier's own e-mails, cost of money |
| `buyer/policy.py` | per thread: anchor by goal and signals, a share of the gap per round, held after a deep first concession, a patience budget for near-cost, fully booked and relationship-goal suppliers; adopts a quoted package when it beats our plan at equal value to the supplier, mirrors a better alternative, takes or offers an index clause; the supplier's asks from its fixed sentences (volume, proof, faster payment, our target); claims 3 in round 1, then 1 per round; deduplicates forecasts from the same period and suppresses unchanged offers; evaluates explicit supplier needs as complete, must-have-safe packages only when total cost improves; closes on final offer, agreement or round limit |
| `buyer/writer.py`, `buyer/llm.py` | the e-mail: a model paragraph answering the supplier's last e-mail and asks (no digits, IDs or leaks, else a deterministic fallback), then code sentences with figures, claims and the proposal; forecast rows as CSV when proof is asked; tracks model attempts, successes, timeouts, rejections and deadline skips |
| `buyer/runner.py` | one message at a time per session, to the thread whose 60 s clock has run longest; keepalive questions for finished bidders; rollback when the arena refuses a send; a non-repeating fallback for failed policy moves; the model's time budgeted so every live clock gets a message; Live Final waves never raise and resume a crashed case |

## Subagent team

Before negotiation, `buyer/research.py` assigns four specialists to supplier data groups and has a
lead choose up to two allowed term trades, claim order and tone. `buyer/rehearsal.py` prepares
possible supplier arguments and evidence-based responses. During negotiation,
`buyer/analyst.py` classifies each reply for tone and tactic; code still controls price and terms.
After a case, `buyer/memory.py` writes a debrief to `buyer/lessons.jsonl` for later research. All
model output is bounded and validated; failures fall back to code-owned behavior.

## Supplier estimate

`arena_kit.cost.supplier_value` prices a deal for the supplier from `standard`, `interest_rate`,
`ppm` and `extra`; `relationship_cost` needs `full_cost`. We estimate full cost from
`should_cost` moved by its drivers' index change, capped at the quote less the sustainable margin
in relationship goals; cost of money from owner type, cash signals and cash discounts; overtime
from capacity signals. The Sunday release (`data/release-sunday/`) and the case's own `facts` are
read at runtime through the ID index.

[agentic-approach.md](agentic-approach.md) is a proposal for a model-chosen tactic inside these
boundaries; not implemented.
# Buyer architecture: the running system

Checked against `main` at `185ad65` on 10 October 2026. This page explains the implemented buyer. [Design](design.md) describes planned work; [learnings](learnings.md) records what practice showed; [system review](system-review.md) lists risks to investigate.

The buyer tries to minimize total cost over the case horizon. Unit price is only one part of that cost: uncovered demand, payment, freight, delivery, quality, tooling, index clauses and sometimes supplier relationship cost also matter. The final action is one accepted term sheet or a walk-away.

## System map

The supplied diagram shows the live negotiation and what happens after it. The runner owns the session and clocks; the negotiator owns decisions for one case. The model can help write a paragraph, while code sets the offer and closing action.

![Simplified buyer system map, from supplier data and negotiation through arena results and human review](assets/system-map.png)

## Example: one supplier quote

This is an **illustrative routine case**, not a recorded session. Suppose we need 1,000 units, the supplier quotes €100 per unit, the buyer's alternative costs €110,000, and the selected non-price terms stay the same as the quote. The supplier has no special signals that change the usual price path.

1. **Arena → Runner.** The arena opens the case with the supplier's email and quote. The runner fetches the quote, starts one `Negotiator` for the case, and watches the supplier's 60 second reply clock.
2. **Data package → Side → Cost engine.** The negotiator reads supplier facts and quote terms. Its `Side` remembers this supplier's quote, profile and planned terms. The cost engine checks the allowed options and must-haves. In this simple example, the routine opening anchor is 82% of the comparable €100 quote, so the first sheet offers **€82 per unit**.
3. **Writer → Arena.** Code puts €82 and the complete term sheet in the email, plus up to three verified claim sentences if the data supports them. The optional model may write a short paragraph; it cannot change the sheet or figures. The runner sends the message to the arena.
4. **Supplier reply → Negotiator.** Suppose the supplier counters at **€95** with the same terms. `Side` records that counter. With no special rule triggered, the policy moves 30% of the €13 gap from our €82 offer toward €95: **€85.90**. The writer sends this next sheet, with at most one new claim.
5. **Close gate → Arena.** Suppose the supplier later makes **€90** its standing final sheet. The buyer does not accept on price alone. If `total_cost` values that complete sheet at €98,000, it meets every must-have, and the alternative is €110,000, the close gate accepts it. If no standing sheet passes those checks, it walks away. With several suppliers, it chooses the cheapest valid standing sheet across them.
6. **Trace → Human review.** The runner saves its decision notes; `buyer pull` collects the arena trace and official cost breakdown. The team compares the result with the best possible cost and tests the next change offline or in the sandbox.

The runner sends one message at a time within a case and serves the supplier whose reply has waited longest. Cases run in parallel during a wave. It limits the optional model to 15 seconds, stops negotiating 90 seconds before a final wave cap, and rereads arena state after a send or close returns HTTP 409.

## What each box does

| Box | Plain-language role | Where it lives |
|---|---|---|
| **Arena** | Supplies the case, opening quotes, supplier replies and final result. The kit handles API calls, session state and quote attachments. | `arena_kit.client`, `arena_kit.play`, [API brief](api.md) |
| **Runner** | Opens cases, chooses which supplier needs a reply, sends one message at a time within a case, watches clocks and runs final waves in parallel. | [`buyer/runner.py`](../buyer/runner.py), [`buyer/cli.py`](../buyer/cli.py) |
| **Data package** | Read-only supplier records, citable facts and documents. The Sunday release joins ID lookup; the package's SQL database stays separate. | `arena_kit.data.DataPackage`, [`buyer/claims.py`](../buyer/claims.py), [`buyer/personas.py`](../buyer/personas.py) |
| **Negotiator** | Owns one case's policy: sets up suppliers, reads replies, plans offers, selects claims and chooses the close action. | `Negotiator` in [`buyer/policy.py`](../buyer/policy.py) |
| **Side** | Remembers one supplier's quote, standard terms, profile, planned terms, offers, counters, asks and pending message. | `Side` in [`buyer/policy.py`](../buyer/policy.py) |
| **Cost engine** | Uses the kit's published cost function, estimates supplier value, searches allowed term combinations and rejects unacceptable deals. | [`buyer/economics.py`](../buyer/economics.py), `arena_kit.cost` |
| **Optional model** | Writes one middle paragraph in the email. It does not choose prices, terms, claims or accept actions. | [`buyer/llm.py`](../buyer/llm.py) |
| **Writer** | Assembles the code-chosen proposal, figures and cited claims into an email; prepares the model brief and template fallback. | [`buyer/writer.py`](../buyer/writer.py), `Negotiator.send` |
| **Close gate** | Finds the cheapest acceptable *standing* supplier sheet or walks away. It checks must-haves and estimated cost against the alternative. | `Negotiator.best_offer`, `Negotiator.close`, `economics.deal_cost` |
| **Trace and back office** | Hold the arena's full conversation, result and official cost breakdown after a session. | `buyer pull` in [`buyer/cli.py`](../buyer/cli.py) |
| **Human review** | Compares decisions with the result, records a finding, changes code and tests again. This is outside the live agent. | [`learnings.md`](learnings.md), [`analysis/explore.py`](../analysis/explore.py) |

### What is binding

The kit's `complete_offer` fills normal planned sheets to the case's negotiable fields. When mirroring a supplier alternative, `economics.quoted_offer` preserves its exact effective package instead of snapping its values. At close, `economics.deal_cost` requires a price, `must_haves_ok` and cost below the buyer's alternative. Its cost uses `arena_kit.total_cost` with this buyer's supplier estimate, so an unknown full cost can make the relationship charge uncertain.

Only the first supplier sheet in its latest reply is a standing sheet that can be accepted. A better alternative sheet must first be sent back so the supplier makes it standing. The model's paragraph is nonbinding, but its wording still matters; [system review](system-review.md) covers the missing central outbound check.

## Every Python file in `buyer/`

| File | Responsibility and main interfaces |
|---|---|
| [`__init__.py`](../buyer/__init__.py) | Marks `buyer` as the package. It contains only a package docstring and makes no decisions. |
| [`cli.py`](../buyer/cli.py) | Command entry point. `main` parses `play`, `run` and `pull`; `load_package` builds the shared ID index; `pull` saves completed sessions, traces and back office. It also selects the kit's naive baseline when requested. |
| [`runner.py`](../buyer/runner.py) | Live orchestration. `play_case` schedules supplier turns and sends messages; `writer_budget` protects clocks; `close` retries a refused close; `play_all` runs practice cases; `play_waves` polls and runs final waves; `save` writes run notes. |
| [`policy.py`](../buyer/policy.py) | The negotiation state machine. `Side` stores one supplier's state; `Negotiator.setup` builds its plan, `move` responds to a reply, `next_price` paces concessions, `pick` chooses claims, `send` assembles a move, `commit` and `rollback` track delivery, and `best_offer` and `close` choose the final action. `asks` reads fixed-form email requests. |
| [`economics.py`](../buyer/economics.py) | All cost and term math. `cost` wraps the kit's total cost; `estimate` models supplier economics; `plan_terms` scores allowed packages; `value` and `price_for_value` compare packages at equal supplier value; `quoted_offer` validates an exact supplier package; `relationship_optimum` handles cases where a lower price raises relationship cost; `deal_cost` is the accept gate. |
| [`claims.py`](../buyer/claims.py) | The citable argument bank. `ClaimBank` looks up facts and IDs, builds sentences about should-cost, orders, indexes, forecasts, notice, supplier notes, scorecards and rival quotes, then ranks them through `for_supplier`. `rival_offer` cites another bidder's current standing sheet. |
| [`personas.py`](../buyer/personas.py) | Supplier reading. `supplier_texts` gathers notes, letters, news and quote remarks; `signals_in` detects traits such as cash need or full capacity; `profile` derives owner, country, signals, cost of money and email tone. Unknown suppliers get a neutral profile. |
| [`writer.py`](../buyer/writer.py) | Email composition. `describe` names the code-chosen terms; `statements` writes binding volume or fixed-payment answers; `facts` and `brief` constrain what the model may say; `email` combines paragraph, claims and proposal; `keepalive_message` handles a waiting bidder. |
| [`llm.py`](../buyer/llm.py) | Optional model connection. `complete_from_env` builds the chat-completions caller; `paragraph` enforces a 15 second wall-clock ceiling and drops output with digits, IDs or leak phrases. The template works when no model is configured or the call fails. |

The buyer wraps `arena_kit`; it does not patch it. [`design.md`](design.md) separates planned agent components from this implemented path. [`system-review.md`](system-review.md) records the failure paths and improvement order. [A more agentic buyer](agentic-approach.md) proposes one bounded next step.
# Learnings

## Louis subagent-team practice batch (2026-10-11)

One hosted Practice session was run for each available case. All ten reached a deal; the mean
score was 0.7772. The dashboard reference at the time was 0.802, but this single batch is not a
paired comparison and does not establish a reliable gain or regression.

| Case | Score |

## Cost (`rules`)

- The category goal sets the rates: fallback risk leverage 3 %, routine 5 %, quality_first 8 %,
  stabilise 10 %, secure_supply 25 %; a relationship charge only in stabilise (sustainable margin

  missing margin points, so C has a minimum below the sustainable margin (D01: 2 points below its
  4 %). It also moves with payment terms (P02: 5,483 at 368.70 and 90 days, 901 at 366.41 and
  14 days).
- Uncovered need costs `fallback_unit_price` plus the risk rate; coverage is
  `min(volume, need) x min(months / 12, horizon)`. Volume above the need is bought anyway; months
  beyond the horizon neither cost nor earn.
- Index clause: `spend x material_share x (|path| - deadband)`, signed like `index_paths`, plus
  `index_risk_pct` of `spend x material_share` whenever a clause exists. A higher price with a
  clause can cost less in C than a lower fixed price: P18 5.40 at a 5 % deadband 259,116.84
  against 5.30 at 0 % 259,970.83 (`9b63768bad5febe5`).
- Late delivery: `late_cost_per_day x days beyond need_lead_time_days`. Must-haves can cap the
  lead time (P05: 42 days).
- Effective date: units before it cost the current price (D01 at 50.90: April instead of
  December start, 0.73 to 0.81; plus 60-day payment, 0.87). Our money: 8 %/yr, reference 60 days;

# Agent design

What the buyer does today. Observations behind it are in `learnings.md`; the module map with
every file is `architecture.md`; the diagram is on page 1 of [how-it-works.pdf](how-it-works.pdf).

## Principle

Code owns every number and every binding decision; the model reads replies and writes words.
Score is total cost C, not price. Every step has a fallback that still sends a move within 60 s.

## A case

1. **Prepare**: open the session, read the quote and standard terms, build the supplier's
   profile and the claim bank, estimate its full cost and cost of money, plan the opening terms
   and price.
2. **Negotiate**, one thread per supplier, in parallel. Each round: read the reply (its sheets,
   asks, signals), plan candidate sheets with `total_cost` and `must_haves_ok`, decide counter,
   accept or walk, write the e-mail (model paragraph with a hard timeout, template if late),
   guard every field and claim, send.
3. **Close**: accept the best standing sheet that keeps every must-have and beats C_alt, or walk;
   at the latest 90 s before the wave's 8-minute cap.

## Modules

| Module | Job |
|---|---|
| `buyer/economics.py` | C of a sheet; the accept gate; a quoted package kept exactly as quoted (`quoted_offer`); what a sheet is worth to the supplier (`supplier_value`, overtime for faster delivery); term planning: every allowed combination priced at the supplier's valuation, lowest C, ties to the supplier's side; the relationship-optimal price; the index-clause trade (the supplier's clause value capped at 8 % of the price, none for a hedged supplier) |
| `buyer/claims.py` | claim bank: should-cost below its price, our order prices, each cost driver's largest fall over any window up to 12 months, notice period, forecast, scorecard, case rival quotes, hedge and open-book notes; rival offers in an RFQ |
| `buyer/personas.py` | owner type, persona signals from notes, letters, quote remarks, news and the supplier's own e-mails, cost of money |
| `buyer/policy.py` | per thread: anchor by goal and signals, a share of the gap per round, held after a deep first concession, a patience budget for near-cost, fully booked and relationship-goal suppliers; adopts a quoted package when it beats our plan at equal value to the supplier, mirrors a better alternative, takes or offers an index clause; the supplier's asks from its fixed sentences (volume, proof, faster payment, our target); claims 3 in round 1, then 1 per round; deduplicates forecasts from the same period and suppresses unchanged offers; evaluates explicit supplier needs as complete, must-have-safe packages only when total cost improves; closes on final offer, agreement or round limit |
| `buyer/writer.py`, `buyer/llm.py` | the e-mail: a model paragraph answering the supplier's last e-mail and asks (no digits, IDs or leaks, else a deterministic fallback), then code sentences with figures, claims and the proposal; forecast rows as CSV when proof is asked; tracks model attempts, successes, timeouts, rejections and deadline skips |
| `buyer/runner.py` | one message at a time per session, to the thread whose 60 s clock has run longest; keepalive questions for finished bidders; rollback when the arena refuses a send; a non-repeating fallback for failed policy moves; the model's time budgeted so every live clock gets a message; Live Final waves never raise and resume a crashed case |

## Subagent team

Before negotiation, `buyer/research.py` assigns four specialists to supplier data groups and has a
lead choose up to two allowed term trades, claim order and tone. `buyer/rehearsal.py` prepares
possible supplier arguments and evidence-based responses. During negotiation,
`buyer/analyst.py` classifies each reply for tone and tactic; code still controls price and terms.
After a case, `buyer/memory.py` writes a debrief to `buyer/lessons.jsonl` for later research. All
model output is bounded and validated; failures fall back to code-owned behavior.

## Supplier estimate

`arena_kit.cost.supplier_value` prices a deal for the supplier from `standard`, `interest_rate`,
`ppm` and `extra`; `relationship_cost` needs `full_cost`. We estimate full cost from
`should_cost` moved by its drivers' index change, capped at the quote less the sustainable margin
in relationship goals; cost of money from owner type, cash signals and cash discounts; overtime
from capacity signals. The Sunday release (`data/release-sunday/`) and the case's own `facts` are
read at runtime through the ID index.

# Buyer architecture: the running system

Checked against `main` at `185ad65` on 10 October 2026. This page explains the implemented buyer. [Design](design.md) describes planned work; [learnings](learnings.md) records what practice showed; [system review](system-review.md) lists risks to investigate.

The buyer tries to minimize total cost over the case horizon. Unit price is only one part of that cost: uncovered demand, payment, freight, delivery, quality, tooling, index clauses and sometimes supplier relationship cost also matter. The final action is one accepted term sheet or a walk-away.

## System map

The supplied diagram shows the live negotiation and what happens after it. The runner owns the session and clocks; the negotiator owns decisions for one case. The model can help write a paragraph, while code sets the offer and closing action.

![Simplified buyer system map, from supplier data and negotiation through arena results and human review](assets/system-map.png)

## Example: one supplier quote

This is an **illustrative routine case**, not a recorded session. Suppose we need 1,000 units, the supplier quotes €100 per unit, the buyer's alternative costs €110,000, and the selected non-price terms stay the same as the quote. The supplier has no special signals that change the usual price path.

1. **Arena → Runner.** The arena opens the case with the supplier's email and quote. The runner fetches the quote, starts one `Negotiator` for the case, and watches the supplier's 60 second reply clock.
2. **Data package → Side → Cost engine.** The negotiator reads supplier facts and quote terms. Its `Side` remembers this supplier's quote, profile and planned terms. The cost engine checks the allowed options and must-haves. In this simple example, the routine opening anchor is 82% of the comparable €100 quote, so the first sheet offers **€82 per unit**.
3. **Writer → Arena.** Code puts €82 and the complete term sheet in the email, plus up to three verified claim sentences if the data supports them. The optional model may write a short paragraph; it cannot change the sheet or figures. The runner sends the message to the arena.
4. **Supplier reply → Negotiator.** Suppose the supplier counters at **€95** with the same terms. `Side` records that counter. With no special rule triggered, the policy moves 30% of the €13 gap from our €82 offer toward €95: **€85.90**. The writer sends this next sheet, with at most one new claim.
5. **Close gate → Arena.** Suppose the supplier later makes **€90** its standing final sheet. The buyer does not accept on price alone. If `total_cost` values that complete sheet at €98,000, it meets every must-have, and the alternative is €110,000, the close gate accepts it. If no standing sheet passes those checks, it walks away. With several suppliers, it chooses the cheapest valid standing sheet across them.
6. **Trace → Human review.** The runner saves its decision notes; `buyer pull` collects the arena trace and official cost breakdown. The team compares the result with the best possible cost and tests the next change offline or in the sandbox.

The runner sends one message at a time within a case and serves the supplier whose reply has waited longest. Cases run in parallel during a wave. It limits the optional model to 15 seconds, stops negotiating 90 seconds before a final wave cap, and rereads arena state after a send or close returns HTTP 409.

## What each box does

| Box | Plain-language role | Where it lives |
|---|---|---|
| **Arena** | Supplies the case, opening quotes, supplier replies and final result. The kit handles API calls, session state and quote attachments. | `arena_kit.client`, `arena_kit.play`, [API brief](api.md) |
| **Runner** | Opens cases, chooses which supplier needs a reply, sends one message at a time within a case, watches clocks and runs final waves in parallel. | [`buyer/runner.py`](../buyer/runner.py), [`buyer/cli.py`](../buyer/cli.py) |
| **Data package** | Read-only supplier records, citable facts and documents. The Sunday release joins ID lookup; the package's SQL database stays separate. | `arena_kit.data.DataPackage`, [`buyer/claims.py`](../buyer/claims.py), [`buyer/personas.py`](../buyer/personas.py) |
| **Negotiator** | Owns one case's policy: sets up suppliers, reads replies, plans offers, selects claims and chooses the close action. | `Negotiator` in [`buyer/policy.py`](../buyer/policy.py) |
| **Side** | Remembers one supplier's quote, standard terms, profile, planned terms, offers, counters, asks and pending message. | `Side` in [`buyer/policy.py`](../buyer/policy.py) |
| **Cost engine** | Uses the kit's published cost function, estimates supplier value, searches allowed term combinations and rejects unacceptable deals. | [`buyer/economics.py`](../buyer/economics.py), `arena_kit.cost` |
| **Optional model** | Writes one middle paragraph in the email. It does not choose prices, terms, claims or accept actions. | [`buyer/llm.py`](../buyer/llm.py) |
| **Writer** | Assembles the code-chosen proposal, figures and cited claims into an email; prepares the model brief and template fallback. | [`buyer/writer.py`](../buyer/writer.py), `Negotiator.send` |
| **Close gate** | Finds the cheapest acceptable *standing* supplier sheet or walks away. It checks must-haves and estimated cost against the alternative. | `Negotiator.best_offer`, `Negotiator.close`, `economics.deal_cost` |
| **Trace and back office** | Hold the arena's full conversation, result and official cost breakdown after a session. | `buyer pull` in [`buyer/cli.py`](../buyer/cli.py) |
| **Human review** | Compares decisions with the result, records a finding, changes code and tests again. This is outside the live agent. | [`learnings.md`](learnings.md), [`analysis/explore.py`](../analysis/explore.py) |

### What is binding

The kit's `complete_offer` fills normal planned sheets to the case's negotiable fields. When mirroring a supplier alternative, `economics.quoted_offer` preserves its exact effective package instead of snapping its values. At close, `economics.deal_cost` requires a price, `must_haves_ok` and cost below the buyer's alternative. Its cost uses `arena_kit.total_cost` with this buyer's supplier estimate, so an unknown full cost can make the relationship charge uncertain.

Only the first supplier sheet in its latest reply is a standing sheet that can be accepted. A better alternative sheet must first be sent back so the supplier makes it standing. The model's paragraph is nonbinding, but its wording still matters; [system review](system-review.md) covers the missing central outbound check.

## Every Python file in `buyer/`

| File | Responsibility and main interfaces |
|---|---|
| [`__init__.py`](../buyer/__init__.py) | Marks `buyer` as the package. It contains only a package docstring and makes no decisions. |
| [`cli.py`](../buyer/cli.py) | Command entry point. `main` parses `play`, `run` and `pull`; `load_package` builds the shared ID index; `pull` saves completed sessions, traces and back office. It also selects the kit's naive baseline when requested. |
| [`runner.py`](../buyer/runner.py) | Live orchestration. `play_case` schedules supplier turns and sends messages; `writer_budget` protects clocks; `close` retries a refused close; `play_all` runs practice cases; `play_waves` polls and runs final waves; `save` writes run notes. |
| [`policy.py`](../buyer/policy.py) | The negotiation state machine. `Side` stores one supplier's state; `Negotiator.setup` builds its plan, `move` responds to a reply, `next_price` paces concessions, `pick` chooses claims, `send` assembles a move, `commit` and `rollback` track delivery, and `best_offer` and `close` choose the final action. `asks` reads fixed-form email requests. |
| [`economics.py`](../buyer/economics.py) | All cost and term math. `cost` wraps the kit's total cost; `estimate` models supplier economics; `plan_terms` scores allowed packages; `value` and `price_for_value` compare packages at equal supplier value; `quoted_offer` validates an exact supplier package; `relationship_optimum` handles cases where a lower price raises relationship cost; `deal_cost` is the accept gate. |
| [`claims.py`](../buyer/claims.py) | The citable argument bank. `ClaimBank` looks up facts and IDs, builds sentences about should-cost, orders, indexes, forecasts, notice, supplier notes, scorecards and rival quotes, then ranks them through `for_supplier`. `rival_offer` cites another bidder's current standing sheet. |
| [`personas.py`](../buyer/personas.py) | Supplier reading. `supplier_texts` gathers notes, letters, news and quote remarks; `signals_in` detects traits such as cash need or full capacity; `profile` derives owner, country, signals, cost of money and email tone. Unknown suppliers get a neutral profile. |
| [`writer.py`](../buyer/writer.py) | Email composition. `describe` names the code-chosen terms; `statements` writes binding volume or fixed-payment answers; `facts` and `brief` constrain what the model may say; `email` combines paragraph, claims and proposal; `keepalive_message` handles a waiting bidder. |
| [`llm.py`](../buyer/llm.py) | Optional model connection. `complete_from_env` builds the chat-completions caller; `paragraph` enforces a 15 second wall-clock ceiling and drops output with digits, IDs or leak phrases. The template works when no model is configured or the call fails. |

## Cost (`rules`)

- The category goal sets the rates: fallback risk leverage 3 %, routine 5 %, quality_first 8 %,
  stabilise 10 %, secure_supply 25 %; a relationship charge only in stabilise (sustainable margin
  0.5 to 8 %) and secure_supply (4 to 10 %). The charge grows with the square of the first 5
  missing margin points, so C has a minimum below the sustainable margin (D01: 2 points below its
  4 %). It also moves with payment terms (P02: 5,483 at 368.70 and 90 days, 901 at 366.41 and
  14 days).
- Uncovered need costs `fallback_unit_price` plus the risk rate; coverage is
  `min(volume, need) x min(months / 12, horizon)`. Volume above the need is bought anyway; months
  beyond the horizon neither cost nor earn.
- Index clause: `spend x material_share x (|path| - deadband)`, signed like `index_paths`, plus
  `index_risk_pct` of `spend x material_share` whenever a clause exists. A higher price with a
  clause can cost less in C than a lower fixed price: P18 5.40 at a 5 % deadband 259,116.84
  against 5.30 at 0 % 259,970.83 (`9b63768bad5febe5`).
- Late delivery: `late_cost_per_day x days beyond need_lead_time_days`. Must-haves can cap the
  lead time (P05: 42 days).
- Effective date: units before it cost the current price (D01 at 50.90: April instead of
  December start, 0.73 to 0.81; plus 60-day payment, 0.87). Our money: 8 %/yr, reference 60 days;
  30 days earlier costs 0.67 % of spend.
- Every session returns C_best and our cost breakdown with the supplier's true numbers; a
  relationship charge reveals its full cost. D01: at most 48.9. Nordmark: C at 358.00 (2,251,140)
  and at 361.67 (2,248,062) with the same clause and payment give its cost of money as about 0
  and its full cost as about 371.7, so C has its minimum near 361 for that structure; the record
  0.847 has a structure these two points do not explain.
- No alternative, so a walk-away scores 0: D01, P05, P06, P10, P14, P17. Contract length or volume
  is ours to pick in 14 of 21 cases. Only a standing sheet can be accepted (an alternative
  returns 422); a better alternative sent back as our sheet became standing (P10).
- The kit's `complete_offer` snaps values and can replace an explicit allowed `None` with the
  first option (`economics.quoted_offer` keeps a quoted package as quoted).

135	        # a bundle's should-cost is unknown: one component's cost is not the price unit of the kit
136	        parts = case.get("parts") or []
137	        full_cost, own_plant = (
138	            safe(lambda: self.full_cost(parts[0], sid), (None, False)) if len(parts) == 1 else (None, False)
139	        )
140	        lead = quote.get("lead_time_days") or s.std.get("lead_time_days")
141	        overtime = 0.005 if "capacity_full" in s.prof["signals"] else 0.001
142	        s.est = eco.estimate(
143	            case, s.std or quote, s.prof["rate"], full_cost, safe(lambda: self.real_ppm(sid)), lead, overtime
144	        )
145	        q_price = quote["unit_price"]
146	        goal, signals = case["buyer"].get("category_goal"), s.prof["signals"]
147	        sustainable = case["buyer"].get("sustainable_margin_pct") or 0
148	        if full_cost and goal in eco.RELATIONSHIP_GOALS:
149	            # it quoted with its margin: a should-cost above that is our estimate's error (P02: 374.95
150	            # against a quote of 370.96; the relationship charge of the deals says about 368)
151	            full_cost = min(full_cost, eco.value(case, quote, s.est) * (1 - sustainable / 100))
152	            s.est["full_cost"] = full_cost
153	        ratio = ANCHOR.get(goal, 0.85)
154	        near_cost = bool(own_plant and full_cost >= 0.98 * q_price)  # it sells at our cost estimate
155	        if goal in eco.RELATIONSHIP_GOALS:
156	            s.budget = 0.3
157	        if "price_frozen" in signals:
158	            ratio = max(ratio, 0.95)  # its list price does not move far; a deep cut only costs patience
159	        if "capacity_full" in signals:
160	            ratio, s.budget = max(ratio, 0.93), min(s.budget, 0.16)
161	        if near_cost:
162	            ratio, s.budget = max(ratio, 0.97), min(s.budget, 0.14)
163	        current = case["buyer"].get("current_unit_price")
164	        if case.get("type") == "price_increase" and current:
165	            ratio = min(ratio, current / q_price)  # a price increase opens at today's price at most
166	        ratio = max(ANCHOR_MIN, ratio)
167	        if brief:
168	            self.apply(s, brief)
169	        # terms planned at the price we open with: coverage pays off at a low price, not at the quote
170	        planned = safe(lambda: eco.plan_terms(case, s.std, s.est, quote, q_price * ratio))
171	        s.terms = planned[0] if planned else eco.complete_offer(case, eco.at_price(quote, q_price * ratio))
172	        s.anchor = s.terms["unit_price"]
173	        s.quote = safe(
174	            lambda: round(eco.price_for_value(case, s.terms, s.est, eco.value(case, quote, s.est)), 2), q_price
175	        )
176	        if full_cost:
177	            # also for a supplier selling at our cost estimate: below the optimum a lower price costs
178	            # us more than it saves, and pushing on made Nordmark withdraw (P02 v1)
179	            s.target = safe(lambda: eco.relationship_optimum(case, s.terms, s.std, s.est, full_cost * 0.85, s.quote))
180	        safe(lambda: self.trade_clause(s, quote, full_cost))
181	        s.claims = safe(lambda: self.bank.for_supplier(sid, q_price), [])
182	        order = brief.get("claim_order") or []  # the arguments the lead expects this supplier to accept, first
183	        s.claims.sort(key=lambda c: order.index(c["kind"]) if c["kind"] in order else len(order))
184	        self.note(
185	            sid,
186	            "setup",
187	            quote=quote,
188	            std=s.std,
189	            profile=s.prof,
190	            full_cost=full_cost,
191	            near_cost=near_cost,
192	            terms=s.terms,
193	            quote_at_terms=s.quote,
194	            anchor=s.anchor,
195	            target=s.target,
196	            budget=s.budget,
197	            claims=[c["text"] for c in s.claims],
198	        )
199	        return s

201	    def apply(self, s, brief):
202	        """The research team's brief on this thread: the lead's trades wait for our opening sheet,
203	        the demo bidding's playbook for the supplier's arguments; notes and tone go to the e-mail
204	        writer. Prices and pace stay with the policy: a model moving them cost score (D01, D02,
205	        P04, `docs/learnings.md`)."""
206	        s.research = brief.get("notes") or ""
207	        s.trades = brief.get("trades") or []
208	        s.playbook = brief.get("playbook") or {}
209	        if brief.get("tone"):
210	            s.prof["warm"] = brief["tone"] == "warm"
211	        self.note(
212	            s.sid,
213	            "research",
214	            trades=s.trades,
215	            reason=brief.get("reason"),
216	            playbook=s.playbook,
217	            findings=brief.get("findings"),
218	        )

220	    def trade_sheets(self, s, main):
221	        """The lead's trades as extra sheets next to our opening sheet `main`: each changes one
222	        term and carries the price at which it costs us exactly what `main` costs, so whichever
223	        the supplier picks, we lose nothing and learn what it values. A trade whose price would
224	        sit at or above what the supplier quotes for those terms, or far below it, is not offered."""
225	        case, out = self.case, []
226	        c_main = eco.cost(case, main, s.std, s.est)
227	        for trade in s.trades:
228	            terms = {**main, trade["field"]: trade["value"]}
229	            if terms == main or not eco.must_haves_ok(case, terms, s.std):
230	                continue
231	            lo, hi = 0.0, main["unit_price"] * 3
232	            if (
233	                not eco.cost(case, eco.at_price(terms, lo), s.std, s.est)
234	                < c_main
235	                < eco.cost(case, eco.at_price(terms, hi), s.std, s.est)
236	            ):
237	                continue
238	            for _ in range(50):  # C rises with the price
239	                mid = (lo + hi) / 2
240	                lo, hi = (mid, hi) if eco.cost(case, eco.at_price(terms, mid), s.std, s.est) < c_main else (lo, mid)
241	            sheet = eco.at_price(terms, int(lo * 100) / 100)
242	            quoted = eco.price_for_value(case, terms, s.est, eco.value(case, eco.at_price(s.terms, s.quote), s.est))
243	            if not TRADE_MIN * quoted <= sheet["unit_price"] < 0.995 * quoted:
244	                continue
245	            out.append(sheet)
246	            self.note(s.sid, "trade_sheet", trade=trade, price=sheet["unit_price"], quoted=round(quoted, 2))
247	        return out

249	    def trade_clause(self, s, quote, full_cost):
250	        """An index clause the supplier values more than it costs us (its driver rose over the
251	        year, the case's path is small): offer it from the start at the price worth the same to it
252	        as our anchor without it, and in a relationship goal no lower than the relationship
253	        optimum, where it is agreed at once (P02: Nordmark agreed to a 5 % copper deadband 4 %
254	        below its fixed price). No trade where its value equals our cost (P08, P18)."""
255	        case = self.case
256	        if "index_clause" not in case["negotiable"] or quote.get("index_clause"):
257	            return
258	        if "hedged" in s.prof["signals"]:
259	            return  # its material is bought forward at fixed prices: the index does not reach its costs
260	        for clause in case.get("term_options", {}).get("index_clause") or []:
261	            if clause and clause.get("series") not in s.est["index_moves"]:
262	                move = self.bank.move12(clause["series"])
263	                if move is not None:
264	                    s.est["index_moves"][clause["series"]] = move
265	        clause = eco.clause_trade(case, s.est)
266	        if not clause or s.terms.get("index_clause") == clause:
267	            return
268	        target_value = eco.value(case, s.terms, s.est)  # our anchor as it is worth to the supplier
269	        terms = {**s.terms, "index_clause": clause}
270	        price = eco.price_for_value(case, terms, s.est, target_value)
271	        floor = None
272	        if full_cost and case["buyer"].get("category_goal") in eco.RELATIONSHIP_GOALS:
273	            floor = eco.relationship_optimum(case, terms, s.std, s.est, full_cost * 0.85, s.quote)
274	            price = max(price, floor or 0.0)
275	        if not eco.must_haves_ok(case, eco.at_price(terms, price), s.std):
276	            return
277	        s.terms = eco.at_price(terms, price)
278	        s.anchor = s.terms["unit_price"]
279	        s.target = floor or s.target
280	        self.note(s.sid, "clause_trade", clause=clause, anchor=s.anchor, target=s.target)

282	    def full_cost(self, part, sid):
283	        """(should-cost of the part, whether it models this supplier's own plant): full cost
284	        without margin. A generic estimate (a German cost base) says little about one supplier."""
285	        rows = self.bank.query("SELECT id, supplier_id, unit_cost FROM should_cost WHERE part_id = ?", (part,))
286	        own = [r for r in rows if r.get("supplier_id") == sid]
287	        if own:
288	            return own[0]["unit_cost"], True
289	        generic = [r for r in rows if not r.get("supplier_id")]
290	        if generic:
291	            return generic[0]["unit_cost"], False
292	        for ref in self.bank.ids("cost:"):  # the case's own facts (no table rows)
293	            f = self.bank.fact(ref)
294	            if f and f.get("part") == part and f.get("unit_cost"):
295	                return f["unit_cost"], f.get("supplier") == sid
296	        return None, False

298	    def real_ppm(self, sid):
299	        """The defect rate it really delivers (latest scorecard), what a chargeback costs it."""
300	        ids = self.bank.ids(f"sc:{sid.split(':')[-1]}@")
301	        f = self.bank.fact(ids[-1]) if ids else None
302	        return f.get("ppm") if f else None

304	    def restore(self, sid, events):
305	        """A resumed session (a crash, a restart): rebuild what we sent and what it answered from
306	        the thread, so the next move continues the path instead of opening at the anchor again."""
307	        s = self.sides[sid]
308	        ours = [m for m in events if m.get("from") == "buyer" and m.get("term_sheets")]
309	        if s.state == "ended" or not ours:
310	            return
311	        s.terms = eco.complete_offer(self.case, ours[-1]["term_sheets"][0]["terms"])
312	        theirs = None
313	        for m in events:
314	            if m.get("from") == "buyer":
315	                refs = m.get("refs") or []
316	                self.used.update(refs)
317	                s.used_claim_families.update(
318	                    family for ref in refs for family in self.claim_families({"kind": "forecast", "ids": [ref]})
319	                )
320	                if m.get("term_sheets"):
321	                    sent_sheets = [sh.get("terms") or {} for sh in m["term_sheets"]]
322	                    s.last_sent_terms = dict(sent_sheets[0])
323	                    s.offered_trade_keys.update(self.trade_keys(sent_sheets))
324	                    price = self.their_price(s, m["term_sheets"][0]["terms"])
325	                    s.ours.append(price)
326	                    s.gaps.append(max(0.0, (theirs - price) / theirs) if theirs else 0.0)
327	            else:
328	                sheets = m.get("term_sheets") or []
329	                if sheets and sheets[0].get("terms", {}).get("unit_price") is not None:
330	                    theirs = self.their_price(s, sheets[0]["terms"])
331	                    if s.ours:
332	                        s.theirs.append(theirs)
333	        if events and events[-1].get("from") != "buyer" and s.theirs:
334	            s.theirs.pop()  # the latest reply is read by move() like any fresh reply
335	        self.note(sid, "restore", ours=s.ours, theirs=s.theirs, terms=s.terms)

338	    def read_signals(self, s, body):
339	        """Persona traits in its own e-mail (a supplier the package does not know, or news since):
340	        merged into the profile; a cash need raises what money now is worth to it."""
341	        new = [k for k in signals_in(body) if k not in s.prof["signals"]]
342	        if not new:
343	            return
344	        s.prof["signals"] = sorted(s.prof["signals"] + new)
345	        if "cash_need" in new:
346	            s.prof["rate"] = round(s.prof["rate"] + 0.05, 3)
347	            if s.est:
348	                s.est["interest_rate"] = s.prof["rate"]
349	        self.note(s.sid, "signals", new=new)

351	    def listen(self, s, body):
352	        """The live analyst on its latest e-mail: the mood goes to the writer, the tactic paces our
353	        next price and our evidence, the argument it recognised picks our prepared answer, its
354	        asks join what the patterns found. Its time comes out of the writer's; late or off, the
355	        move goes on with the patterns alone."""
356	        s.mood, s.tactic, s.argument = None, None, 0
357	        if self.writer_s < ANALYST_MIN_S:  # several threads share the clocks: the move comes first
358	            return
359	        t0 = time.monotonic()
360	        arguments = s.playbook.get("arguments") or []
361	        seen = analyst.read(self.complete, self.case, body, s.ours, s.theirs, arguments, self.writer_s / 2)
362	        self.writer_s -= time.monotonic() - t0
363	        if seen is None:
364	            return
365	        s.asks = [k for k in ASKS if k in s.asks or k in seen["asks"]]
366	        s.mood, s.tactic, s.argument, s.live = seen["mood"], seen["tactic"], seen["argument"], seen["notes"]
367	        s.tactics.append(s.tactic)
368	        self.note(s.sid, "analyst", seconds=round(time.monotonic() - t0, 1), **seen)

370	    def team_facts(self, s, first, extra):
371	        """What the team adds to the writer's facts: our prepared answer to the argument its e-mail
372	        made, a weak point to press in the opening, the trades on offer, the mood to meet."""
373	        out = []
374	        rebuttals = s.playbook.get("rebuttals") or []
375	        if s.argument and s.argument <= len(rebuttals) and rebuttals[s.argument - 1]:
376	            out.append(
377	                f'they argue: "{s.playbook["arguments"][s.argument - 1]}" Our answer, in your own words: '
378	                f"{rebuttals[s.argument - 1]}"
379	            )
380	        if first and s.playbook.get("press"):
381	            out.append(f"a point to raise politely, once: {s.playbook['press'][0]}")
382	        if extra:
383	            why = "; ".join(t["why"] for t in [*s.trades, *s.active_trades] if t.get("why"))
384	            out.append(
385	                "our proposal lists alternative packages after the first one: say they are free to choose the "
386	                f"one that suits them best ({why})"
387	            )
388	        elif s.active_trades:
389	            why = "; ".join(t["why"] for t in s.active_trades if t.get("why"))
390	            out.append(f"we adjusted the package in response to {why}; explain the commercial terms clearly")
391	        if s.mood == "irritated":
392	            out.append("they sound irritated: acknowledge it sincerely before anything else")
393	        elif s.mood == "pressured":
394	            out.append("they sound under pressure: be calm and make the next step easy for them")
395	        return out

397	    def their_price(self, s, terms):
398	        """Its sheet as a price at our planned terms (same value to it)."""
399	        same = all(terms.get(k) == v for k, v in s.terms.items() if k != "unit_price" and k in terms)
400	        if same:
401	            return terms["unit_price"]
402	        v = eco.value(self.case, terms, s.est)
403	        return round(eco.price_for_value(self.case, s.terms, s.est, v), 2)

405	    def switch(self, s, new, why):
406	        """Plan new non-price terms; our last price moves to the same value for the supplier."""
407	        if s.ours:
408	            v = eco.value(self.case, eco.at_price(s.terms, s.ours[-1]), s.est)
409	            s.ours[-1] = round(eco.price_for_value(self.case, new, s.est, v), 2)
410	        if s.theirs:
411	            v = eco.value(self.case, eco.at_price(s.terms, s.theirs[-1]), s.est)
412	            s.theirs[-1] = round(eco.price_for_value(self.case, new, s.est, v), 2)
413	        s.terms = {**new}
414	        self.note(s.sid, "switch_terms", why=why, terms={k: v for k, v in new.items() if k != "unit_price"})
415	
416	    def adopt(self, s, sheets):
417	        """Compare complete quoted packages, then switch once to the cheapest useful one."""
418	        if not s.ours:
419	            return
420	        case = self.case
421	        standing = sheets[0]["terms"]
422	        planned_cost = eco.cost(case, eco.at_price(s.terms, self.their_price(s, standing)), s.std, s.est)
423	        candidates = []
424	        for sheet in sheets:
425	            new = eco.quoted_offer(case, sheet["terms"], s.std)
426	            if new is None or all(new.get(k) == v for k, v in s.terms.items() if k != "unit_price"):
427	                continue
428	            c = eco.deal_cost(case, new, s.std, s.est)
429	            if c is not None and c < planned_cost - max(1.0, 0.001 * planned_cost):
430	                candidates.append((c, new))
431	        if candidates:
432	            _, new = min(candidates, key=lambda row: (row[0], repr(sorted(row[1].items()))))
433	            self.switch(s, new, "complete quoted package costs us less")

435	    # -- one move ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
436	    def move(self, sid, threads, writer_s=llm.TIMEOUT_S):
437	        """The next message to this supplier: {"message": ...}, or None when the thread is done.
438	        `writer_s`: what the supplier clocks leave for the model paragraph."""
439	        s, events = self.sides[sid], threads[sid]
440	        self.writer_s = writer_s
441	        s.prev_state = s.state
442	        last = latest(events)
443	        status = last.get("status")
444	        if s.state == "ended" or status in ENDED:
445	            s.state = "ended"
446	            return None
447	        sheets = [sh for sh in last.get("term_sheets") or [] if sh.get("terms", {}).get("unit_price") is not None]
448	        if not sheets:
449	            s.state = "ended" if not standing(events)[0] else "done"
450	            return None
451	        std_before = s.std
452	        s.std = standard_terms(events) or s.std
453	        fresh = s.last_reply is not last
454	        if fresh:
455	            terms_before = dict(s.terms)
456	            estimate_before = dict(s.est)
457	            self.adopt(s, sheets)
458	            s.term_change = any(sheets[0]["terms"].get(k, v) != v for k, v in terms_before.items() if k != "unit_price")
459	            s.theirs.append(self.their_price(s, sheets[0]["terms"]))
460	            s.last_sheet = sheets[0]["terms"]
461	            s.last_reply = last
462	            s.asks = asks(last.get("body"))
463	            self.read_signals(s, last.get("body"))
464	            if self.briefs is not None and status not in DONE:
465	                self.listen(s, last.get("body"))
466	            economics_changed = s.terms != terms_before or s.est != estimate_before or s.std != std_before
467	            if s.target is not None and economics_changed:
468	                s.target = eco.relationship_optimum(
469	                    self.case,
470	                    s.terms,
471	                    s.std,
472	                    s.est,
473	                    s.est["full_cost"] * 0.85,
474	                    max(s.est["full_cost"] * 0.85, s.quote, s.target, s.theirs[-1]),
475	                )
476	        theirs = s.theirs[-1]
477	        if s.state in ("mirror", "closing"):  # we sent its own sheet or our target: done
478	            s.state = "done"
479	            return None
480	        left = self.moves_left(s, events)
481	        if status in DONE or left <= 0:
482	            return self.finish(s, sheets, events, theirs, left)
483	        if s.ours and s.target and theirs <= s.target:
484	            # relationship goal: below the target a lower price costs more than it saves
485	            s.state = "closing"
486	            sheet = eco.at_price(s.terms, max(s.target, theirs))
487	            if self.same_offer(s.last_sent_terms, sheet):
488	                s.state = "done"
489	                self.note(sid, "no_progress", reason="relationship target already offered")
490	                return None
491	            return self.send(s, [sheet], [], events, theirs)
492	        if s.ours and theirs <= s.ours[-1]:  # it came below what we offered: take it
493	            return self.finish(s, sheets, events, theirs, left)
494	        price, n_claims = self.next_price(s, theirs)
495	        claims = self.pick(s, n_claims, threads)
496	        sheets = [eco.at_price(s.terms, price)]
497	        if not s.ours and s.trades:
498	            sheets += safe(lambda: self.trade_sheets(s, sheets[0]), [])[:2]
499	        elif s.ours:
500	            sheets += safe(lambda: self.need_trade_sheets(s, sheets[0]), [])[:2]
501	        switched_trade_keys = set()
502	        if self.same_offer(s.last_sent_terms, sheets[0]):
503	            if len(sheets) == 1:
504	                s.state = "done"
505	                self.note(sid, "no_progress", reason="unchanged price and terms")
506	                return None
507	            # Do not resend the old primary sheet. Move the thread onto the best new package,
508	            # whose buyer cost is lower and whose estimated supplier value matches the main offer.
509	            switched_trade_keys = self.trade_keys(sheets)
510	            sheet = sheets[1]
511	            old_target = s.target
512	            self.switch(s, sheet, "cost-checked response to a supplier need")
513	            if old_target is not None and s.est.get("full_cost"):
514	                floor = s.est["full_cost"] * 0.85
515	                s.target = eco.relationship_optimum(
516	                    self.case,
517	                    s.terms,
518	                    s.std,
519	                    s.est,
520	                    floor,
521	                    max(floor, s.quote, old_target, s.theirs[-1]),
522	                )
523	            sheets = [sheet]
524	        result = self.send(s, sheets, claims, events, theirs)
525	        if s.pending and switched_trade_keys:
526	            s.pending["trade_keys"].update(switched_trade_keys)
527	        return result
